sanskrit: tato no yudhyamānānāṃ paraṃ śaktyā suyodhana saindhavo nihato rājan daivam atra paraṃ smṛtam
english: Then, O Suyodhana, while we fought with the utmost of our power, the lord of the Sindhus was slain, O king; in this, destiny is reckoned the highest cause.

sanskrit: paraṃ yatnaṃ kurvatāṃ ca tvayā sārdhaṃ raṇājire hatvāsmākaṃ pauruṣaṃ hi daivaṃ paścāt karoti naḥ satataṃ ceṣṭamānānāṃ nikṛtyā vikrameṇa ca
english: Though we strove our utmost together with you on the field of battle, destiny undid our manly valor and set us behind, for all our ceaseless striving with both cunning and prowess.

sanskrit: daivopasṛṣṭaḥ puruṣo yat karma kurute kva cit kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ sma tat tasya daivena vinihanyate
english: Whatever deed a man assailed by destiny may anywhere perform, that deed, once done, is undone again for him by destiny.

sanskrit: yat kartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa vyavasāyavatā satā tat kāryam aviśaṅkena siddhir daive pratiṣṭhitā
english: What is to be done by a man who is resolute and true, that he must do without misgiving; but success rests upon destiny.

sanskrit: nikṛtyā nikṛtāḥ pārthā viṣayogaiś ca bhārata dagdhā jatugṛhe cāpi dyūtena ca parājitāḥ
english: By trickery the sons of Pṛthā were cheated, O Bhārata, and by poisoned draughts, and they were nearly burned in the house of lac, and they were vanquished at dice.

sanskrit: rājanītiṃ vyapāśritya prahitāś caiva kānanam yatnena ca kṛtaṃ yat te daivena vinipātitam
english: By recourse to statecraft they were sent away to the forest; yet whatever was thus contrived by effort was cast down by destiny.

sanskrit: yudhyasva yatnam āsthāya mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam yatatas tava teṣāṃ ca daivaṃ mārgeṇa yāsyati
english: Fight on, taking up your effort, and make death your only turning-back; as you strive and as they strive, destiny will go its own appointed way.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ matipūrvaṃ hi sukṛtaṃ dṛśyate kva cit duṣkṛtaṃ tava vā vīra buddhyā hīnaṃ kurūdvaha
english: No deliberate good deed of theirs is anywhere to be seen, nor any wicked deed of yours, O hero, devoid of judgment, O upholder of the Kurus.

sanskrit: daivaṃ pramāṇaṃ sarvasya sukṛtasyetarasya vā ananyakarma daivaṃ hi jāgarti svapatām api
english: Destiny is the measure of every deed, good or otherwise; for destiny, whose work cannot be turned aside, keeps watch even over those who sleep.

sanskrit: bahūni tava sainyāni yodhāś ca bahavas tathā na tathā pāṇḍuputrāṇām evaṃ yuddham avartata
english: Many were your armies and many likewise your warriors—not so those of the sons of Pāṇḍu; and yet the battle went thus.

sanskrit: tair alpair bahavo yūyaṃ kṣayaṃ nītāḥ prahāriṇaḥ śaṅke daivasya tat karma pauruṣaṃ yena nāśitam
english: By those few you many strikers have been brought to ruin; I think this is the work of destiny, by which manly valor has been brought to naught.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇānāṃ bahu tat taj janādhipa pāṇḍavānām anīkāni samadṛśyanta saṃyuge
english: Saṃjaya said: While they were conversing thus at length on this and that, O lord of men, the battalions of the Pāṇḍavas appeared before them in the fray.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ vyatiṣaktarathadvipam tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ sārdhaṃ rājan durmantrite tava
english: Then began the battle, chariots and elephants locked together, between your men and their foes, O king, through your own ill counsel.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tad udīrṇagajāśvaughaṃ balaṃ tava janādhipa pāṇḍusenām abhidrutya yodhayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: That host of yours, O lord of men, with its surging flood of elephants and horses, rushed upon the army of the Pāṇḍavas and gave it battle on every side.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ kuravaś caiva yodhayantaḥ parasparam yamarāṣṭrāya mahate paralokāya dīkṣitāḥ
english: The Pāñcālas and the Kurus, fighting one another, were as men consecrated for the great realm of Yama, for the world beyond.

sanskrit: śūrāḥ śūraiḥ samāgamya śaratomaraśaktibhiḥ vivyadhuḥ samare tūrṇaṃ ninyuś caiva yamakṣayam
english: Heroes closing with heroes pierced one another swiftly in the fight with arrows, lances, and spears, and led each other to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: rathināṃ rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ rudhirasrāvi dāruṇam prāvartata mahad yuddhaṃ nighnatām itaretaram
english: Between car-warriors and car-warriors a great and terrible battle, streaming with blood, broke out as they struck one another down.

sanskrit: vāraṇāś ca mahārāja samāsādya parasparam viṣāṇair dārayām āsuḥ saṃkruddhāś ca madotkaṭāḥ
english: And the elephants, O great king, closing upon one another, enraged and frenzied with rut, gored each other with their tusks.

sanskrit: hayārohān hayārohāḥ prāsaśaktiparaśvadhaiḥ bibhidus tumule yuddhe prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ
english: Horsemen pierced horsemen with darts, spears, and battle-axes in the tumultuous fight, each seeking great renown.

sanskrit: pattayaś ca mahābāho śataśaḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ anyonyam ārdayan rājan nityayattāḥ parākrame
english: And the foot-soldiers, O mighty-armed one, by the hundreds, weapons in hand, harried one another, O king, ever intent upon valor.

sanskrit: gotrāṇāṃ nāmadheyānāṃ kulānāṃ caiva māriṣa śravaṇād dhi vijānīmaḥ pāñcālān kurubhiḥ saha
english: By the names of their lineages and their families, O venerable one, heard upon the field, we knew the Pāñcālas apart from the Kurus.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ samare yodhāḥ śaraśaktiparaśvadhaiḥ preṣayan paralokāya vicaranto hy abhītavat
english: In the fray the warriors, ranging about without fear, sent one another to the world beyond with arrows, spears, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: śarair daśa diśo rājaṃs teṣāṃ muktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ na bhrājanta yathāpūrvaṃ bhāskare 'staṃ gate 'pi ca
english: By the arrows loosed in their thousands, O king, the ten quarters of the sky, even after the sun had set, no longer shone as before.

sanskrit: tathā prayudhyamāneṣu pāṇḍaveyeṣu nirbhayaḥ duryodhano mahārāja vyavagāhata tad balam
english: While the Pāṇḍava warriors were thus fighting on, Duryodhana, undaunted, O great king, plunged into that host.

sanskrit: saindhavasya vadhenaiva bhṛśaṃ duḥkhasamanvitaḥ martavyam iti saṃcintya prāviśat tu dviṣadbalam
english: Sorely stricken with grief at the slaying of the lord of the Sindhus, and resolving that he too must die, he entered the army of the foe.

sanskrit: nādayan rathaghoṣeṇa kampayann iva medinīm abhyavartata putras te pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Making the air resound with the rumble of his chariot and seeming to shake the earth, your son advanced against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulas tasya teṣāṃ ca bhārata abhavat sarvasainyānām abhāvakaraṇo mahān
english: That tumultuous clash between him and them, O Bhārata, became a great wreaking of destruction upon all the troops.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdinagataṃ sūryaṃ pratapantaṃ gabhastibhiḥ tathā tava sutaṃ madhye pratapantaṃ śarormibhiḥ
english: As the noonday sun blazing with its rays, so blazed your son in their midst with his waves of arrows.

sanskrit: na śekur bhārataṃ yuddhe pāṇḍavāḥ samavekṣitum palāyane kṛtotsāhā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye
english: The Pāṇḍavas could not even look upon that descendant of Bharata in the fight; their spirit roused only to flight, they had lost all heart for victory over the foe.

sanskrit: paryadhāvanta pāñcālā vadhyamānā mahātmanā rukmapuṅkhaiḥ prasannāgrais tava putreṇa dhanvinā ardyamānāḥ śarais tūrṇaṃ nyapatan pāṇḍusainikāḥ
english: The Pāñcālas, slaughtered by the great-souled one, ran about in flight; and harried swiftly by the gold-feathered, keen-pointed arrows of your son the bowman, the Pāṇḍava soldiers fell.

sanskrit: na tādṛśaṃ raṇe karma kṛtavantas tu tāvakāḥ yādṛśaṃ kṛtavān rājā putras tava viśāṃ pate
english: Not such a feat in battle did your men perform as the king, your son, performed, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: putreṇa tava sā senā pāṇḍavī mathitā raṇe nalinī dviradeneva samantāt phullapaṅkajā
english: By your son that Pāṇḍava army was churned in the battle, like a lotus-pool with its blooming lilies trampled on every side by an elephant.

sanskrit: kṣīṇatoyānilārkābhyāṃ hatatviḍ iva padminī babhūva pāṇḍavī senā tava putrasya tejasā
english: Like a lotus-pond robbed of its splendor when its waters fail and the wind and sun assail it, so became the Pāṇḍava army through the fiery might of your son.

sanskrit: pāṇḍusenāṃ hatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tava putreṇa bhārata bhīmasenapurogās tu pāñcālāḥ samupādravan
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍava army stricken by your son, O Bhārata, the Pāñcālas, with Bhīmasena at their head, rushed upon him.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaṃ daśabhir mādrīputrau tribhis tribhiḥ virāṭadrupadau ṣaḍbhiḥ śatena ca śikhaṇḍinam
english: He pierced Bhīmasena with ten arrows, the two sons of Mādrī with three each, Virāṭa and Drupada with six, and Śikhaṇḍin with a hundred.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca saptatyā dharmaputraṃ ca saptabhiḥ kekayāṃś caiva cedīṃś ca bahubhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna with seventy, the son of Dharma with seven, and the Kekayas and the Cedis with many whetted arrows.

sanskrit: sātvataṃ pañcabhir viddhvā draupadeyāṃs tribhis tribhiḥ ghaṭotkacaṃ ca samare viddhvā siṃha ivānadat
english: Having pierced the Sātvata with five, the sons of Draupadī with three each, and Ghaṭotkaca in the battle, he roared like a lion.

sanskrit: śataśaś cāparān yodhān sadvipāśvarathān raṇe śarair avacakartograiḥ kruddho 'ntaka iva prajāḥ
english: And other warriors by the hundreds, with their elephants, horses, and chariots, he cut down in the fight with cruel arrows, like wrathful Death cutting down living beings.

sanskrit: tasya tān nighnataḥ śatrūn rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahad dhanuḥ bhallābhyāṃ pāṇḍavo jyeṣṭhas tridhā ciccheda māriṣa
english: As he was striking down those foes, the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas cut his great gold-backed bow into three with two broad-headed shafts, O venerable one.

sanskrit: vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhiḥ samyagastaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ marmāṇi bhittvā te sarve saṃbhagnāḥ kṣitim āviśan
english: And he pierced him with ten well-aimed, sharpened arrows; but all of these, after piercing his vital parts, broke and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ pramuditā yodhāḥ parivavrur yudhiṣṭhiram vṛtrahatyai yathā devāḥ parivavruḥ puraṃdaram
english: Then the gladdened warriors gathered round Yudhiṣṭhira, as the gods gathered round Puraṃdara for the slaying of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tava putrasya māriṣa śaraṃ paramadurvāraṃ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge sa tena bhṛśasaṃviddho niṣasāda rathottame
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira loosed at your son in the fray an arrow most hard to ward off, O venerable one; and grievously pierced by it, your son sank down upon his splendid chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālasainyānāṃ bhṛśam āsīd ravo mahān hato rājeti rājendra muditānāṃ samantataḥ
english: Then from the Pāñcāla troops there rose a great loud clamor on every side, O lord of kings, as they rejoiced, crying, 'The king is slain!'

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdaravaś cograḥ śuśruve tatra māriṣa atha droṇo drutaṃ tatra pratyadṛśyata saṃyuge
english: And a fierce din of the twang of arrows was heard there, O venerable one; then Droṇa swiftly appeared upon that field.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭo duryodhanaś cāpi dṛḍham ādāya kārmukam tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti rājānaṃ bruvan pāṇḍavam abhyayāt
english: And Duryodhana, heartened, taking up his stout bow, advanced upon King Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava, crying, 'Stand, stand!'

sanskrit: pratyudyayus taṃ tvaritāḥ pāñcālā rājagṛddhinaḥ tān droṇaḥ pratijagrāha parīpsan kurusattamam caṇḍavātoddhatān meghān nighnan raśmimuco yathā
english: The Pāñcālas, eager for the king, swiftly went out against him; but Droṇa received them, seeking to save the best of the Kurus, as the ray-shedding sun beats back clouds driven up by a fierce gale.

sanskrit: tato rājan mahān āsīt saṃgrāmo bhūrivardhanaḥ tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca sametānāṃ yuyutsayā
english: Then, O king, there was a great battle, swelling ever larger, between your men and their foes, all met together in their lust for combat.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yat tadā prāviśat pāṇḍūn ācāryaḥ kupito vaśī uktvā duryodhanaṃ samyaṅ mama śāstrātigaṃ sutam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the self-controlled preceptor, in his wrath, entered among the Pāṇḍavas, having justly rebuked my son Duryodhana for transgressing his counsel—

sanskrit: praviśya vicarantaṃ ca raṇe śūram avasthitam kathaṃ droṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ paryavārayan
english: how did the Pāṇḍavas surround Droṇa, that mighty archer, the hero, as he ranged and stood firm in the battle he had entered?

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakram ācāryasya mahātmanaḥ ke cottaram arakṣanta nighnataḥ śātravān raṇe
english: Who guarded the right wheel of the great-souled preceptor, and who guarded the left, as he slew his foes in the fight?

sanskrit: nṛtyan sa rathamārgeṣu sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ dhūmaketur iva kruddhaḥ kathaṃ mṛtyum upeyivān
english: Dancing along the chariot-paths, that foremost of all who bear arms, wrathful like a comet, how did he come to meet his death?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sāyāhne saindhavaṃ hatvā rājñā pārthaḥ sametya ca sātyakiś ca maheṣvāso droṇam evābhyadhāvatām
english: Saṃjaya said: In the late afternoon, having slain the lord of the Sindhus, the son of Pṛthā, joining the king, and Sātyaki, that great archer—the two rushed upon Droṇa himself.

sanskrit: tathā yudhiṣṭhiras tūrṇaṃ bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ pṛthak camūbhyāṃ saṃsaktau droṇam evābhyadhāvatām
english: Likewise Yudhiṣṭhira swiftly, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, each engaged with his own division, rushed upon Droṇa himself.

sanskrit: tathaiva nakulo dhīmān sahadevaś ca durjayaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śatānīko virāṭaś ca sakekayaḥ matsyāḥ śālveyasenāś ca droṇam eva yayur yudhi
english: So too the wise Nakula and the unconquerable Sahadeva, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śatānīka, and Virāṭa with the Kekayas, the Matsyas and the Śālveya troops—all went against Droṇa in the fight.

sanskrit: drupadaś ca tathā rājā pāñcālair abhirakṣitaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnapitā rājan droṇam evābhyavartata
english: And King Drupada too, guarded all about by the Pāñcālas, the father of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king, advanced upon Droṇa himself.

sanskrit: draupadeyā maheṣvāsā rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ sasenās te 'bhyavartanta droṇam eva mahādyutim
english: The sons of Draupadī, those mighty archers, and the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, together with their troops, advanced upon Droṇa of great splendor.

sanskrit: prabhadrakāś ca pāñcālāḥ ṣaṭsahasrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ droṇam evābhyavartanta puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam
english: And the Prabhadraka Pāñcālas, six thousand strikers strong, advanced upon Droṇa, with Śikhaṇḍin set at their head.

sanskrit: tathetare naravyāghrāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ sahitāḥ saṃnyavartanta droṇam eva dvijarṣabham
english: So too the other tigers among men, the great car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, banded together and turned upon Droṇa, that bull among the twice-born.

sanskrit: teṣu śūreṣu yuddhāya gateṣu bharatarṣabha babhūva rajanī ghorā bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinī
english: When those heroes had gone forth to battle, O bull of the Bhāratas, there came on a dreadful night, deepening the terror of the timid.

sanskrit: yodhānām aśivā raudrā rājann antakagāminī kuñjarāśvamanuṣyāṇāṃ prāṇāntakaraṇī tadā
english: For the warriors it was a baleful, terrible night, O king, bound for the abode of Death, making an end of the lives of elephants, horses, and men.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ ghorāyāṃ nadantyaḥ sarvataḥ śivāḥ nyavedayan bhayaṃ ghoraṃ sajvālakavalair mukhaiḥ
english: In that dreadful night the jackals, howling on every side with flaming gobbets in their mouths, gave warning of a terrible peril.

sanskrit: ulūkāś cāpy adṛśyanta śaṃsanto vipulaṃ bhayam viśeṣataḥ kauravāṇāṃ dhvajinyām atidāruṇam
english: And owls too appeared, foretelling vast terror, most dire of all in the host of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tataḥ sainyeṣu rājendra śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān bherīśabdena mahatā mṛdaṅgānāṃ svanena ca
english: Then among the armies, O lord of kings, there arose a great din, with the mighty sound of kettledrums and the boom of tabors,

sanskrit: gajānāṃ garjitaiś cāpi turaṅgāṇāṃ ca heṣitaiḥ khuraśabdanipātaiś ca tumulaḥ sarvato 'bhavat
english: and with the trumpeting of elephants and the neighing of horses and the clatter of falling hooves, a tumult arose on every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ saṃdhyāyām atidāruṇam droṇasya ca mahārāja sṛñjayānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then in the twilight there broke out a most dreadful battle, O great king, between Droṇa and the Sṛñjayas on every hand.

sanskrit: tamasā cāvṛte loke na prājñāyata kiṃ cana sainyena rajasā caiva samantād utthitena ha
english: When the world was wrapped in darkness, nothing whatever could be discerned, with the dust raised up on every side by the host.

sanskrit: narasyāśvasya nāgasya samasajjata śoṇitam nāpaśyāma rajo bhaumaṃ kaśmalenābhisaṃvṛtāḥ
english: The blood of man and horse and elephant ran mingled together; we could no longer see the dust of the earth, shrouded as it was by the gore.

sanskrit: rātrau vaṃśavanasyeva dahyamānasya parvate ghoraś caṭacaṭāśabdaḥ śastrāṇāṃ patatām abhūt
english: As of a thicket of bamboo burning by night upon a mountain, so arose a fearful crackling sound from the weapons that fell.

sanskrit: naiva sve na pare rājan prājñāyanta tamovṛte unmattam iva tat sarvaṃ babhūva rajanīmukhe
english: Neither one's own men nor the foe could be told apart, O king, in that enveloping darkness; at the onset of night the whole field became as if maddened.

sanskrit: bhaumaṃ rajo 'tha rājendra śoṇitena praśāmitam śātakaumbhaiś ca kavacair bhūṣaṇaiś ca tamo 'bhyagāt
english: The dust of the earth, O lord of kings, was laid by the blood; but with the golden mail and ornaments the darkness was lit up.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā bhāratī senā maṇihemavibhūṣitā dyaur ivāsīt sanakṣatrā rajanyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then that Bhārata host, adorned with gems and gold, was like the star-strewn sky by night, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: gomāyubaḍasaṃghuṣṭā śaktidhvajasamākulā dāruṇābhirutā ghorā kṣveḍitotkruṣṭanāditā
english: It rang with the cries of jackals and ravens, it was thronged with spears and banners, terrible with dreadful howls, resounding with roars and shouts.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavan mahāśabdas tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ samāvṛṇvan diśaḥ sarvā mahendrāśaninisvanaḥ
english: Then there arose a great tumultuous uproar that made the hair stand on end, filling all the quarters, like the crash of mighty Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sā niśīthe mahārāja senādṛśyata bhāratī aṅgadaiḥ kuṇḍalair niṣkaiḥ śastraiś caivāvabhāsitā
english: At midnight, O great king, that Bhārata army was seen lit up with armlets, earrings, golden necklaces, and weapons.

sanskrit: tatra nāgā rathāś caiva jāmbūnadavibhūṣitāḥ niśāyāṃ pratyadṛśyanta meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: There the elephants and the chariots, decked with gold, appeared in the night like clouds shot through with lightning.

sanskrit: ṛṣṭiśaktigadābāṇamusalaprāsapaṭṭiśāḥ saṃpatanto vyadṛśyanta bhrājamānā ivāgnayaḥ
english: Swords, spears, maces, arrows, clubs, darts, and lances, as they fell in showers, were seen flashing like flames of fire.

sanskrit: duryodhanapurovātāṃ rathanāgabalāhakām vāditraghoṣastanitāṃ cāpavidyuddhvajair vṛtām
english: With Duryodhana for its forewind, with chariots and elephants for its thunderheads, thundering with the blare of instruments, hung about with bows for lightning and with banners,

sanskrit: droṇapāṇḍavaparjanyāṃ khaḍgaśaktigadāśanim śaradhārāstrapavanāṃ bhṛśaṃ śītoṣṇasaṃkulām
english: with Droṇa and the Pāṇḍavas for its rain-clouds, with swords, spears, and maces for its thunderbolts, with showers of arrows and missiles for its wind, fraught utterly with cold and heat—

sanskrit: ghorāṃ vismāpanīm ugrāṃ jīvitacchidam aplavām tāṃ prāviśann atibhayāṃ senāṃ yuddhacikīrṣavaḥ
english: that army—dreadful, astounding, fierce, life-severing, with no raft to cross it, most terrible—those who longed to fight entered in.

sanskrit: tasmin rātrimukhe ghore mahāśabdaninādite bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajanane śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhane
english: At that dreadful onset of night, resounding with a great uproar, that bred terror in the timid and swelled the joy of the brave—
